drug_class: Immune checkpoint inhibitor (a type of immunotherapy / cancer medicine)
purpose: Dostarlimab-Gxly is used to treat certain types of cancer, including a type of uterine (endometrial) cancer and other solid tumors that have specific genetic changes. It may be used alone or combined with chemotherapy. Your doctor chose it because your cancer has certain features that make it likely to respond to this treatment.
how_it_works: Your immune system has natural 'brakes' that cancer cells can hijack to hide from it. Dostarlimab works by releasing those brakes — specifically by blocking a protein called PD-1 on your immune cells. Once unblocked, your immune system can recognize and attack the cancer cells more effectively.
common_side_effects: Tiredness or fatigue, nausea, diarrhea, constipation, decreased appetite, rash or itchy skin, low red blood cell count (anemia), and joint or muscle pain. Many patients also experience changes in lab values like blood counts or liver enzymes, so regular blood tests are important.
warnings: Because this medicine revs up your immune system, it can sometimes cause your immune system to attack healthy organs — this can affect your lungs, liver, intestines, kidneys, hormone glands, or other areas. Tell your doctor or nurse RIGHT AWAY if you have new or worsening cough, shortness of breath, severe diarrhea, yellowing of skin or eyes, unusual weight changes, or severe fatigue. Also tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as this medicine can harm an unborn baby. Use effective birth control during treatment and for several months after.
typical_dosing: It is given as an IV infusion (through a vein) at a cancer clinic, usually over about 30 minutes. A common schedule is once every 3 weeks for the first several doses (called cycles), then once every 6 weeks after that. Your doctor will decide the exact schedule and number of treatments based on your specific situation.
